ov: Fish that lure prey with a modified fin ray on the head, tipped with a lure that glows in some species. They live in seas worldwide, from the seabed to the deep open ocean, and include monkfish and frogfish. Their teeth fold back, so prey slides in but can’t escape.
len: Mostly 2–18 cm; European monkfish up to 2 m
df: Other animals, lured within reach of the mouth. All anglerfish are carnivores.
fx: In some deep-sea anglerfish the female can be several orders of magnitude heavier than the male.
Anglerfish can stretch their jaws and stomachs to swallow prey up to twice their own size.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is confirmed for deep-sea anglerfish: males attach to the much larger female (sexual parasitism).
